message: Your attendance rate is critically low. Missing classes directly impacts your understanding of core subjects.
action: Aim to attend all upcoming classes. Catch up on missed notes immediately.

message: Your attendance is moderate. Regular attendance is crucial for academic stability.
action: Try to minimize unnecessary absences to ensure you do not miss important topics.

message: Excellent attendance record! This forms a strong foundation for your academic success.
action: Keep up the great attendance! Use class time to actively participate.

message: You are studying below the recommended minimum for solid academic progress.
action: Increase your self-study time by at least 30-45 minutes each day. Create a structured timetable.

message: You have a strong commitment to studying.
action: Maintain your current study routine, but ensure you take adequate breaks to avoid burnout.

message: High daily screen time can cause cognitive fatigue, reduce focus, and heavily cut into study time.
action: Implement a strict limit on non-academic screen time. Use app blockers.

message: Your screen time is moderately high. This might be a subtle distraction.
action: Try to reduce screen time by 30-60 minutes daily and substitute it with light reading.

message: When you study irregularly or cram at the last minute, your brain struggles to store information.
action: Use the Pomodoro Technique (study for 25 mins, break for 5 mins) and set a Non-Negotiable Daily Study Time.

message: You have excellent study consistency, which is the best scientifically-proven way to retain information.
action: Keep up your regular study rhythm! Consistency is your strongest asset.

message: Your average marks indicate you are struggling significantly with the current curriculum.
action: Urgently seek tutoring or remedial classes. Focus on fundamentally understanding core concepts.

message: Your average marks reflect excellent academic performance and strong comprehension.
action: Keep up the excellent work! Consider taking on more challenging topics.

message: Both your study hours and consistency are critically low. This combination drastically increases the risk of falling behind.
action: Start with a micro-habit: Commit to just 30 minutes of study at the exact same time every single day to build momentum.

message: You are putting in the hours, but your marks remain low. Your current study method is likely ineffective.
action: Switch from passive reading to active recall and past paper practice. Ask your teacher for strategy advice.

message: Your high screen time appears to be directly interfering with your homework completion.
action: Enforce a rule: Homework must be 100% completed before any leisure screen time begins.

message: Your metrics look balanced across the board.
action: Maintain your current routines and continue striving for incremental improvements in your daily habits.
